close_reason: Landed in commit 4ec9135. Per parent sgrr.17 family decision (option (c) doc-only hardening), the kit does not adopt Pref(NonZeroU8) type-level newtypes. New crate-level rustdoc section 'Design: numeric-range bounds are not type-enforced' documents the 13 pref sites + list_as + PartialDate.month/day in one table; README Gotchas list gains a consolidating bullet for all four spec-bounds findings (.14 pref, .15 list_as, .22 PartialDate).
description:
RFC 9553 §1.5.3 defines the common 'pref' attribute as an integer in 1..=100
(lower = more preferred). The crate types every pref field as Option<u32>:
Nickname.pref:185, Pronouns.pref:308, EmailAddress.pref:368,
OnlineService.pref:414, Phone.pref:454, LanguagePref.pref:488,
Calendar.pref:533, SchedulingAddress.pref:567, Address.pref:631,
CryptoKey.pref:713, Directory.pref:761, Link.pref:816, Media.pref:864.

A caller can construct Nickname { pref: Some(0), ... } or Some(101) or
Some(u32::MAX) and serialize a wire-invalid JSContact object. Deserialize
accepts the same. No type-level guarantee, no documented validation contract,
no helper method that returns Result. Every consumer that cares about the bound
will write the same range check.

The same Rust newtype pattern as PrefValue(NonZeroU8) capped at 100 in a sealed
constructor would carry the contract at the type level, with serde
deserialize_into rejecting out-of-range values automatically. That is a
breaking change to ship later (every Option<u32> field becomes Option<PrefValue>),
so it needs to happen before 1.0 or it cannot happen.

Sister concern to JMAP-sgrr.5 (which is about UnsignedInt width 2^32 vs 2^53).
That bead is about the upper bound of the JSON-safe-integer range; this bead
is about the RFC's prescriptive narrower bound.
title: pref fields are u32 but RFC 9553 §1.5.3 specifies 1..=100 — no type-level bound, no validation
